To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) peroxidase and non-specific esterase activities are associated with cotton fiber cell wall fractions, (2) the peroxidase activity is low during the elongation growth phase, and (3) the esterase activity is high during the elongation and low during the secondary thickning phase.
the peroxidase activity is high during the period of secondary thickening of fibers and that esterase activity is high during primary elongation.

In summary, our research is concerned with
a study of the role of peroxidase activity in the development of the cotton fiber cell wall.
the role of peroxidase activity in the synthesis of lignin-like material and the role of esterases in the turnover of wall phenolic compounds during fiber growth.
the role of peroxidases and esterases in the development of cotton fibers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the peroxidase and the esterase fractions are not involved in fiber growth.
the peroxidase and non-specific esterase activities of the wall are involved in the turnover of phenolic compounds that are cross-linked in the wall matrix.
the peroxidase and/or esterase activities in both cytoplamic and wall fractions are not related to the cessation of elongation and initiation of secondary wall thickening in cotton fibers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
esterases are involved in wall metabolism, and the peroxidases are involved in the oxidation and reduction reactions of phenolic acids.
peroxidases and esterases associated with cotton fibers may be involved in the regulation of fiber growth and development.
the increase in peroxidases and esterases during secondary wall thickening is a part of the mechanism of wall modification that occurs at this stage of fiber development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the peroxidase and non-specific esterase activities are not directly related to the growth of cotton fiber.
the peroxidases and esterases associated with the wall fractions may be important in the turnover and/or cross-linking of wall polysaccharide and phenolic acid moieties.
peroxidase and peroxidase-coupled reactions may be involved in the control of fiber growth.
